classification.difficultyReason: Link familiar plot-reading procedures to percentages, descending ranks and ranges across two datasets.

content.prompt: The weights of 40 male and 39 female students are compared in the back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot shown below. The weights are given correct to the nearest kilogram.

spec.description: Central stems between vertical dividers; descending female leaves on the left and ascending male leaves on the right. All supplied leaves, blank rows and the two-digit stem 10 are retained. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.answerVisibility: All leaves, stems, headings and the key are permanent givens.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Find the percentage of males who weigh more than 79 kg.

answer.worked:
There are $10+2+3=15$ males weighing more than 79 kg.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage}&=\frac{15}{40}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage}&=37.5\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Find the percentage of females who weigh less than 50 kg. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
There are $2+9=11$ females weighing less than 50 kg, out of 39 females.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Percentage}&=\frac{11}{39}\times100\%\\\text{Percentage}&=\frac{1100}{39}\%\\\text{Percentage}&\approx28.21\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: i
children.prompt: What are the weights of the 20th and 21st heaviest males?

answer.worked: There are $3+2+10=15$ males weighing at least 80 kg. Counting down through the seventies gives ranks 16–21 as $76,76,75,74,74,73$. The 20th and 21st heaviest males weigh 74 kg and 73 kg, respectively.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: What are the weights of the 20th and 21st heaviest females?

answer.worked: There are $3+5+8=16$ females weighing at least 60 kg. Counting down through the fifties gives ranks 17–21 as $59,58,57,57,57$. The 20th and 21st heaviest females both weigh 57 kg.

children.label: i
children.prompt: What is the difference in weight between the heaviest and lightest males?

answer.worked:
The heaviest male weighs 109 kg and the lightest weighs 52 kg.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Difference}&=109-52\\\text{Difference}&=57\text{ kg}\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: What is the difference in weight between the heaviest and lightest females?

answer.worked:
The heaviest female weighs 81 kg and the lightest weighs 38 kg.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Difference}&=81-38\\\text{Difference}&=43\text{ kg}\end{align*}$$
